title: Repair and Emergency Service Calls — Flat-Rate Billing, Refrigerant Limits and Repair Scope
content:
## Billing standard

**(a) Two lines per repair.** Every repair on a call under Repair and Emergency Service Calls is billed from the price book of the class's price book edition as two lines for its task code. One is a repair parts line at the task's parts amount. The other is a repair labor line at the task's labor amount multiplied by the class's labor multiplier, rounded to the cent half up. A task with no parts amount posts only the labor line.

**(b) Upfront price.** The price quoted from the book and approved by the customer before work begins is final wherever the class's upfront price guarantee holds, even if the job takes longer. It holds in every class.

**(c) Refrigerant.** Refrigerant is billed per pound added, by refrigerant type, at the class's R-410A, R-22 or R-454B price per pound, with no labor multiplier. No more than the class's per-visit pounds may be added on one visit, and never more than the class's R-22 limit of R-22.

**(d) Leak search offer.** When the refrigerant added to the same unit within 12 months would exceed the class's leak-search figure, the refrigerant leak search task must be offered before more is added. The 12 months run as rolling calendar months ending on the date of handling. They count the pounds on the refrigerant lines of every call for that same unit posted in that period. A customer who declines the leak search is still limited to the visit cap.

**(e) Major repairs.** Major repairs (compressor, evaporator coil, condenser coil, reversing valve and TXV replacement) are performed only in classes that allow them. In other classes the technician restores operation where possible. The major repair is then booked as a follow-up Standard Service Call priced at the Standard multiplier.

**(f) Truck stock.** Where a class is limited to parts carried on the truck, a part not carried on the truck is installed on a return visit. That visit carries the class's return-visit fee and no new diagnostic fee.

**(g) Special-order deposit, no longer in force.** The former clause requiring a deposit of the class's special-order parts deposit percentage of the parts amount before special-order parts are ordered is no longer in force. It has been superseded by the current special-order release basis.

**(h) Estimates.** A written estimate stays valid at the quoted price for the class's estimate validity period.

## Worked examples (hypothetical calls)

| Call | Price-book figures | Lines billed |
|---|---|---|
| Blower motor replace, Weekend Service Call (multiplier 1.25) | Parts $342.00, labor $387.00 | Parts $342.00; labor $387.00 multiplied by 1.25, which is $483.75 |
| Condensate drain clear, Standard Service Call (1.0) | No parts amount, labor $159.00 | Labor line only, $159.00 |
| Compressor failure found on an Overnight Emergency Service Call | Major repair | Operation restored where possible. Compressor replacement booked as a follow-up Standard Service Call at the 1.0 multiplier |

## Refrigerant boundary (hypothetical unit)

A unit has had 3 pounds added in the last 12 months, and the class's leak-search figure is 4 pounds. Adding 1 more pound brings the total to exactly 4, which does not exceed the figure. Adding 2 more pounds would bring it to 5, which exceeds the figure, so the leak search must be offered before that refrigerant is added.

superseded_clauses: Special-order parts require a deposit of special_order_parts_deposit_pct of the parts amount before they are ordered.
